subject: Mythology
title: Masks and the Spirit World
description: A quick, practical guide to Masks and the Spirit World.

hook.text: When an African dancer puts on a sacred mask, they do not represent a spirit. They become the spirit.

buildup.text: Masks are carved to channel specific ancestors, gods, or nature spirits during ceremonies and rites of passage.

discovery.text: The Dogon Kanaga mask represents the connection between heaven and earth, worn during funeral dances for the dead.

twist.text: European artists like Picasso saw African masks and changed Western art forever. Cubism was born from sacred objects.

climax.text: Most African masks in Western museums were taken without permission. Repatriation debates are reshaping the art world.

punchline.text: Objects of prayer became art, then objects of political debate.

quiz.question: How did African masks influence Western art?
options: European artists copied the mask patterns for interior design
Picasso and others were inspired by them, leading to Cubism and modern art movements
African artists moved to Europe and opened galleries
